# Check 5: hindcast cross-validation

The hindcast compares the observations of the peeled years with their one-year-ahead predictions from the
retrospective runs (Kell et al. 2016). The mean absolute scaled error (MASE) scales the prediction error by that
of a naive random-walk forecast: MASE < 1 means the model predicts better than the naive forecast. `ss3_hindcast()`
does indices, mean length and mean age, as `ss3diags::SSmase()`.

```{r hc}
data(retro.phk)
hc <- ss3_hindcast(retro.phk)
hc$mase
```

```{r hc-plot, fig.height = 4}
ss3plot_hcxval(hc)
```

```{r hc-sma, fig.height = 5}
ss3plot_hcxval(ss3_hindcast(retro.sma))
```

> **Check 5: prediction skill.** MASE > 1 for an index means the model has no prediction skill for it. With
> indices that vary little the naive error is small and `MAE.base.adj` (default 0.1) limits the scaling.
